messages.subject: Listen - Permission Denied
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I was wondering if I might get some help using the listen function.
I've been having some problems with it. The error I receive is a
"Permission denied" error:

> feebee <- readWave("../Songs/1020/111_T0000112.wav")
> feebee

Wave Object
	Number of Samples:      77634
	Duration (seconds):     1.76
	Samplingrate (Hertz):   44100
	Channels (Mono/Stereo): Mono
	Bit (8/16/24/32):       16

> listen(feebee)
sh: /tmp/RtmpfxUPVm/tuneRtemp.wav: Permission denied
> play(feebee)
Error in play.default(feebee) :
  Argument must be a Sample object or the name of a wav file.

I suspect that this may have more to do with the "play" function,
since when using "play" with a Wave class object, it creates, plays,
then deletes the file. However, as you can see here, when I use the
play function, it doesn't like my Wave object at all.

I can get the file to play by using play("../Songs/
1020/111_T0000112.wav", play). But I'd really like to use listen() so
I can slow the song down.

I know play isn't part of the seewave package, but I thought some of
you might have suggestions anyway.

I'm using R version 2.13.1 (2011-07-08) on Ubuntu 10.10 x64

Thanks!

Steffi LaZerte

messages.subject: Re: Listen - Permission Denied
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jerome,

I don't think this is an ESS/emacs problem because I get the same
error message when I run R in a basic linux terminal (even if I run as
sudo).

I played around a bit more and was trying out savewav and play
functions (because that is how listen and play work, I think. First
saving the wave, then playing it).

Listen has problems with permissions:
> listen(feebee)
sh: /tmp/Rtmpd5HNpQ/tuneRtemp.wav: Permission denied

But no permission problems with savewav:
> savewav(filename="/tmp/Rtmpd5HNpQ/temp.wav", wave=feebee)

And no problems playing the saved file:
> play("/tmp/Rtmpd5HNpQ/temp.wav")

/tmp/Rtmpd5HNpQ/temp.wav:

 File Size: 155k      Bit Rate: 706k
  Encoding: Signed PCM
  Channels: 1 @ 16-bit
Samplerate: 44100Hz
Replaygain: off
  Duration: 00:00:01.76

In:100%  00:00:01.76 [00:00:00.00] Out:77.6k [      |      ] Hd:0.0
Clip:0
Done.

So I think this means that the basic permissions are okay...? But
there is a problem with listen()'s permissions?  I admit that I'm
really not familiar with how R packages and functions work on the
inside.

Any thoughts?

Thanks for all your help!

Steffi LaZerte

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Re: Listen - Permission Denied
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

You are right the problem does not seem to be linked to ESS or emacs. Sorry.

It seems that the package tuneR does not find directly a wav player to
use under Linux.

You need then to specify which player you'd like to use with the
function setWavPlayer(), for instance
setWavPlayer("audacious")

If you want to have it directly done each time you run an R session, add
this line in your .Rprofile file:
options(WavPlayer = "audacious")

You may have some alerts coming back from audacious but the tries I ran
worked quite well from both a terminal and emacs.

Hope this solve the issue,

Best

Jerome

messages.subject: Re: Listen - Permission Denied
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jerome,

Thank you!  That worked for me, although not at first. I confused at
first as to why I couldn't set the wave player, and realized that if
you also load the "sound" library, setWavPlayer() and a couple other
functions are overridden.

So that definitely solved the problem for me, but it might be worth
noting that it won't work if you load the sound library first (I
tested out the order of loading libraries and posted them below).

Thanks again for your time and effort!

Steffi LaZerte

########
## Testing Order
########

library(tuneR)
library(seewave)
library(sound)
feebee <- readWave("/home/steffi/Desktop/019_T0000021.wav")
listen(feebee)  #get error message
setWavPlayer("play")
listen(feebee)  #get error message

library(tuneR)
library(seewave)
feebee <- readWave("/home/steffi/Desktop/019_T0000021.wav")
listen(feebee)  #get error message
setWavPlayer("play")
listen(feebee)  #plays fine
library(sound)
listen(feebee)  #plays fine
